name: Neck Harness Extension
description: The neck harness extension uses a specialized head harness with a chain and weight plate, allowing cervical extension against loaded resistance while standing, seated, or in a hip-hinge position. The harness distributes force evenly around the head and skull, enabling heavier loading than plate-on-head variations while maintaining safety. It is a staple neck-strengthening exercise for combat sports athletes, wrestlers, football players, and lifters seeking maximal posterior cervical strength.

execution.starting_position: Fit the neck harness securely on the head. Attach the chain and weight. Stand or sit with the torso bent forward (hip hinge), or lie prone on a bench. Begin with the head in a neutral or slightly flexed position.
execution.setup_instructions: The neck harness is the specialized equipment required. Begin conservatively and add weight only after several weeks of consistent training at bodyweight neck exercises.
steps: Step 1: Don the neck harness with an appropriate weight attached.
Step 2: Take a hip-hinge or seated position, head hanging forward.
Step 3: Extend the neck upward, bringing the head to a neutral or slightly extended position.
Step 4: Hold briefly at the top.
Step 5: Lower slowly back to the starting position with controlled cervical flexion.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the extension upward, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight before the neck musculature is conditioned
Extending too far back — work to a comfortable, not maximum, range
Using jerky movement — controlled motion is essential
safety_considerations: The neck harness must fit properly before loading — a poor fit can create dangerous force distribution
Build very slowly — weeks of unloaded neck work before adding harness resistance
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Comfortable cervical flexion at the bottom to comfortable extension at the top.
coaching_cues: Don't force range — work to comfortable extension
